items.title: Prefix sum: range queries O(1) mein
items.one_idea: Build a running-total array once in O(n); then the sum of any range left..right is one subtraction, prefix[right+1] - prefix[left], so every query costs O(1) instead of a loop.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: array के किसी हिस्से का sum हर बार loop चलाए बिना कैसे निकालोगे?

items.visual_idea: Six cells 3 1 4 1 5 9 with a second row below filling left to right with running totals 0 3 4 8 9 14 23; then a bracket over indices 2 to 4 lights the two prefix cells 14 and 4 and one subtraction 14 - 4 = 10 appears; last panel compares a loop re-adding the bracket every query with a single subtraction.

items.example: EXAMPLE array [3,1,4,1,5,9]; prefix [0,3,4,8,9,14,23]; sum of indices 2..4 = 10 = 14 - 4; whole array 23. n = 100000 and 100000 queries: worst-case brute force 10,000,000,000 additions vs 100,000 build plus 100,000 subtractions.
items.check_question: With prefix [0,3,4,8,9,14,23], what is the sum of indices 1..3? (6, since 9 - 3)
items.cover_headline: Prefix sum: range sums in O(1)
facts_to_verify: Range sum = prefix[right+1] - prefix[left]; build O(n), query O(1), O(n) space (doocs 0303)

items.title: Pivot Index: left aur right ka sum barabar kahan
items.one_idea: Pivot Index: keep a running left sum and get the right sum as total minus left minus the current element, so the first index where the two sides are equal is found in one O(n) pass with O(1) extra space.
items.spoken_hook: Pivot Index problem: left और right का sum बराबर कहाँ?
items.hook_source: direct_question is the least used of the last six built days (only d008); problem named by its standard name, one plain question, defined in the very next line
items.visual_idea: Array row 1 7 3 6 5 6 with a gold marker walking right; left sum and right sum tiles under it update at every index until both read 11 at index 3 and the cell turns green.
items.everyday_anchor: none: developer audience, no everyday analogies (owner 2026-10-26)
items.example: EXAMPLE array [1,7,3,6,5,6], total 28 (i=0 right=27, i=1 right=20, i=2 right=17, i=3 left=11 right=11) -> index 3. [1,2,3] -> -1. [2,1,-1] -> 0 (empty left side is 0). [1,2,3,3] -> 2. n = 100000: re-summing both sides at every index is about 9,999,900,000 element reads (EXAMPLE, n*(n-1)) vs about 200,000 for the one pass.
items.pattern: running left sum, right = total - left - current
items.check_question: For [1,2,3,3], which index is the pivot? (2)
items.cover_headline: Pivot Index: balance both sides in one pass
facts_to_verify: Problem paraphrased: leftmost index where left sum equals right sum; empty side = 0; none -> -1 (doocs 0724)
One pass, time O(n), space O(1) (doocs 0724)
